description:
FOUND s461ar, PRE-EXISTING, and it is why `re/pat.t` still reads C 0/0 in
baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv after #931 removed its census drop.

tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm sets --control-stack-size but NOT --dynamic-space-size, so
every runner uses SBCL's default 1 GB dynamic space.  `t/re/pat.t` emits a
236 KB .lisp file and SBCL dies COMPILING it:

    Heap exhausted during garbage collection: 0 bytes available, 64 requested.
    ... bytes_allocated = 1026030592 [95.6% of 1073741824 max]
    0: SB-REGALLOC::GROW-SC  1: SB-REGALLOC::PACK-TN  ... 4: SB-C::%COMPILE-COMPONENT

Given `--dynamic-space-size 6144` the same file COMPILES and then dies at load
for a DIFFERENT reason (task #933's `require threads`), so this is the first of
two blockers, not the only one.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST "RAISE THE NUMBER": the scope note in CLAUDE.md says
`--all --jobs 8` can already OOM the 10 GB budget because each worker reserves
a 512 MB control stack AND runs a perl side; multiplying the dynamic space by
six across four to eight workers is exactly the wrong direction.  Measure the
gate's and the sweep's PEAK first (the same measurement the prove-core
MemoryMax filler wants), then decide between: a per-file allowance like
baselines/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv (a `perl-suite-heap.tsv`), a global raise
with a matching jobs cap, or reducing what the compiler emits for a file this
size (pat.t is 1263 perl rows; the emitted top-level form for run_tests is
enormous).

A runner change means the runner row of the what-to-run-when table: run the
changed runner once and compare verdicts file by file, plus PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1
before and after.
subject: t/re/pat.t cannot even COMPILE at the runners' 1 GB SBCL heap: "Heap exhausted" during %COMPILE-COMPONENT
